newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan wants to become Boeing's partner - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wants to become Boeing's partner - paper.

text.p: Taiwan wants to make regional passenger jets in partnership with U.S. aircraft giant Boeing, a newspaper reported on Saturday.
The Commercial Times said Premier Lien Chan on Friday expressed Taiwan's willingness to cooperate with Boeing during a meeting with officials from Washington state, where Boeing is based.
The report did not give specific details.
Taiwan has been looking at cooperation with foreign aerospace companies to produce regional passenger jets.
In 1995, Taiwan Aerospace led five other local firms in signing a contract with U.S.-based Swearingen Aircraft Inc to produce six-seat SJ-30 passenger jets in the United States.
Taiwan Aerospace has said it hoped to take between five and 10 percent of a planned multinational joint venture that aims to manufacture 100-seat passenger jets.
Taiwan Aerospace, 29 percent owned by the Taiwan government, was founded in 1991 as the main vehicle to develop the island's aerospace industry.
